title: The cover letter: Equinix's wrong-document confession, in its own words
dek: The companion piece to Equinix's out-of-time motion - a one-page letter from its senior counsel admitting he filed PJM's document instead of his own protest in ER26-3515.
body_html:
Regulatory filings are usually bloodless. This one is not. Equinix's senior counsel for global regulatory affairs tells the Secretary of the Commission, plainly, that after several failed upload attempts 'I inadvertently attached the wrong document' - the original PJM filing rather than Equinix's protest - and asks that the intended document 'be accepted for the Commission's consideration'.

Two details are worth noting. First, the honesty is strategic: a clean, immediate confession is exactly what makes an out-of-time acceptance easy to grant. Second, the letter reveals how close this came to mattering. If the error had surfaced days later, Equinix - the largest data-center operator in the world - would have had no protest on the record in the docket that will shape its economics for a decade.

For the full story and what happens next, read our analysis of the accompanying out-of-time motion.
key_points: A direct admission of a clerical error, filed with the corrected protest attached.
The 4:20pm rejected submission vs the 4:13pm save timestamp anchors the equity argument.
Companion to the formal out-of-time motion - together they almost certainly cure the miss.
watch: Acceptance of the corrected protest, then whether Equinix's substantive positions align with Google and the Data Center Coalition.
